text: - Rotation: game n -> opponent index ((n-1)//2) % 3 in [full-strength, skill-0, elo-1800-setting]; I am White on odd game numbers, Black on even. So 1-2 full, 3-4 skill-0, 5-6 elo-1800, repeat. 200 games ~ 68/66/66.

- Elo estimator (rating.py): Bradley-Terry-Davidson posterior, anchors skill-0=1320, elo-1800=1800, prior N(1500,800), **window = last 50 rated games**. Full-strength games are uncalibrated (excluded). Final reported Elo depends on roughly the last 75 benchmark games (50 rated).
- Draws by repetition / 50-move rule are claimed automatically. 400 plies = unfinished (not scored, does not count toward 200).
1. Rated games (skill-0, elo-1800) decide Elo: maximize score there. Full-strength games: play solidly, resign only when objectively hopeless; they still count toward 200 but not Elo.

2. My main risks as a language-model player: misreading the board, hanging pieces, missing opponent threats, illegal moves, and draws by repetition/50-move in won positions. The move procedure (procedure.md) targets these.
- **full-strength**: skill 20, 1M nodes ~ very strong (well above 3000). Any inaccuracy is punished.
- skill-0: develop safely, create multiple threats, attack the king; take everything that is free; convert cleanly; never gamble on it responding sensibly. Avoid stalemate/repetition.
- full-strength: solid London/Caro/Slav, trade when possible, no pawn grabs, resign when hopeless.
- full-strength (games 1-2): punished every inaccuracy; found knight-harassment (…Na2) and a mating net with Q+2N. No chances unless I play flawlessly.

Results: full-strength 0-2 (losses, expected). skill-0: 1-1 (G3 loss: hung a knight to a line I opened myself, then hung a rook to a queen diagonal; G4 win). elo-1800: 0-2 (G5: queen trapped on f5, then allowed Qxg2# by skipping the king-safety check; G6: lost queen to a discovered attack, knight to a queen diagonal, then a Q+B mating net).

Evaluation point: after games 7-12 (block 2). Success criteria: zero pieces lost to a one-move capture in rated games; score >= 1.5/2 vs skill-0 and >= 1/2 vs elo-1800; Elo estimate rising over block 2. If the oversight class recurs >= 2 times in block 2, revise (e.g. shorter candidate lists, scan the top-2 candidates fully).

Scan did catch 12...cxb5?? (Qxa3), 15...Nf5 (pinned), 20...Bh6/Bg7 (Bxe7#). Procedure v2.4: reply legality + king-air rule. Review: games/008.md.

Criteria: (1) zero pieces lost to a one-move tactic in rated games — NOT met (G11 back-rank mate, decisive; G10 exchange by sign error; G12 queen-for-rook by forced-reply discovery, not decisive). (2) >= 1.5/2 vs skill-0 — met (2/2). (3) >= 1/2 vs elo-1800 — met (1/2). (4) Elo rising — met.

Observable success criteria at the evaluation point (after game 18): zero material lost to a one-move tactic, including after a forced reply, in games 15-18 (skill-0 and elo-1800); score >= 1.5/2 vs skill-0 and >= 1/2 vs elo-1800 in block 3; Elo estimate after game 18 at or above 1560. - G14 (B, full-strength): LOSS by resignation at move 13 (0 illegal). Caro-Kann Advance, pawn regained by move 10; after 11.b4 Nxb4 12.axb4 I played 12...Bxb4?? and 13.Rxa5 took my queen along the a-file that the a-pawn's departure had just opened. Scan written but line B said "a3 vacated: nothing" — attacker enumeration was by nearby pieces, not by line. Same class as G3/G6/G7. Procedure v2.8: attackers enumerated by line (file, rank, two diagonals, knight hops) for every valuable piece; a pawn capture/advance by the opponent re-opens its file and diagonals, which must be named in line B; and "which of my pieces is attacked right now?" asked before every non-forced move. Review: games/014.md.

Elo after game 16: 1610 (1340-1900), 10 rated games. Review: games/016.md. Procedure v2.9: pawn captures named in A/4a, discovered-check capture in C0, king adjacency in C2, new C4 (check-plus-attack forks on a piece left loose), written file/rank differences before UCI, endgame notes.

Rh1#) and stood a pawn up with Qxc6+/Qxa8 ideas, then 32.gxf3?? Qxf2#: my scan wrote "...Qxf2+ Kxf2" without noticing that gxf3 had vacated g2 and the h2 rook now guarded f2 (king recapture illegal). 32.Rd2 held everything. Criteria: (1) zero one-move losses in games 21-24 — NOT MET (G21 Qa4# net, G22 repetition draw from a won ending, G24 self-blocked defence line and Be7# net); (2) >=1.5/2 vs skill-0 — NOT MET (0.5/2: loss, draw); (3) >=1/2 vs elo-1800 — MET (1/2: win G23, loss G24); (4) Elo after game 24 >= 1560 — NOT MET (1520). Block 4 score 1.5/6 (games 19-20 vs full strength lost). The two-candidate limit and the computed-fact lines were followed, but the failures were omissions of whole lines (line B skipped on a recapture, king-square checks not enumerated, slider paths and defence lines written from memory, four illegal attempts in two games). Decision: Trial 4 = a fixed written table per move (T1-T7, procedure v4.0) in which no line may be skipped and every path or defence line is read from the FEN.

Change: procedure v4.0 replaces the free-form scan with a seven-row table (board from FEN, last move lines, hanging pieces, checks now and after the candidate with flight squares, candidate paths and vacated lines and relied-on defence lines, best reply with forced-sequence replay, repetition ledger in endings). 'Obvious' moves are not exempt. Evaluation point: after game 30. Success criteria: (a) zero illegal attempts in games 25-30; (b) no loss or draw caused by a one-move oversight in a position with equal or better material; (c) >=1.5/2 vs skill-0 (games 27-28); (d) >=1/2 vs elo-1800 (games 29-30); (e) Elo after game 30 >= 1540. Fallback (Trial 5) if (a) or (b) fails: the table is written twice (once before choosing, once after choosing) with the second pass only checking the candidate's T4/T5 rows.
